On August 6, President Trump signed a new executive order targeting certain children born in the United States, including cases involving so-called “birth tourism.” But there’s a major problem: the Supreme Court already ruled on June 30 that children born in the U.S. to parents who are here unlawfully or temporarily are citizens at birth under the 14th Amendment. Then on September 2, a federal judge in Maryland issued a preliminary injunction blocking the administration from denying or refusing to recognize citizenship for people covered by the case. So right now, despite the new executive order, birthright citizenship remains protected for the people covered by the Supreme Court’s ruling. And one more thing: this isn’t something Congress can simply erase with an ordinary law. The Citizenship Clause is part of the Constitution.
